LESSON: TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: AGRICULTURE
Strand: Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship
Topic 3.1: Tools and Equipment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Tools and Equipment, part of Agricultural Technologies and Entrepreneurship in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 AGRICULTURE.

Key inquiry question: How do tools and equipment contribute to efficiency of farm operations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Tools and Equipment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Responsibility: learner demonstrates excellence and self-drive when carrying out agricultural tasks using tools and

equipment and when carrying out maintenance practices on the tools and equipment.

● Respect: learner accommodates other learners’ ideas when analysing tools and equipment for various farm tasks.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Health promotion issues: learner carries first aid in case of accidents when using tools and equipment.

● Social economic and environmental issues: learner observes safety precautions when carrying various farm tasks using

tools and equipment.

Suggested Learning Resources: Sample agricultural tools such as panga, jembe, pruning knife and burdizzo, elastrator and

ring dehorning wire, claw hammer, hand saw (all with padded handles for enhanced grip by the user. They should also be of

varied weights in line with the user’s functional ability), Adapted computers with appropriate accessibility features, Appropriate

applications/ software, Ergonomic and head operated mouse and footboards, Writing resources, Positioning devices, ICT tools

with appropriate accessibility features, Other related services (physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, learner
